text:
alex: Heads-up — I hit an odd perf delta in the benchmark runs this morning. When we switch the kernel-selection rollout to the new heuristics, replay harness p99 is ~18% worse than the synthetic harness for the same traffic trace. Suspect kernel mismatch + KV-cache interaction + client conn churn.
marie: Numbers? which trace and commit?
alex: repro on trace `search-traffic-2026-03-10` + commit d4f2b7. Quick summary: synthetic run -> p50 40ms p95 95ms p99 190ms; replay run -> p50 42ms p95 115ms p99 225ms. (All measured on same Dedicated pool).
sam: Interesting. Did you use the same client settings for both? HTTP keepalive / max-conns / grpc multiplexing can shift tail a lot, especially over TLS. Are you using HTTP/1.1 keepalive or gRPC streams?
alex: Synthetic used a single long-lived connection (kept alive), replay harness opens ~N short-lived connections to simulate sessions (default harness behavior). Kernel selection seems to flip to the "wide-context" kernel variant for replay which increases per-step kernel latency for these seq lengths. Also saw KV-cache eviction spikes in the log.
jon: Can we force the kernel selection to the old variant to gate apples-to-apples? e.g. ENV flag in runtime: `REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=attn_v1` and rerun both harnesses. If p99 lines up then it's clearly kernel selection logic + replay connection patterns exposing cache pressure.
taylor: Also check TCP_NODELAY vs Nagle. If the replay opens many short connections, Nagle + TLS coalesce can add milliseconds per-write. For short tokens, that shows up at the tail.
marie: Steps: 1) pin kernel (jon's env) and run replay vs synthetic 2) add KV cache eviction histogram and per-request KV write latency to tracing 3) run single-conn replay variant to see connection effect
alex: Ran step 1 & 3. When I pin `attn_v1` p99 converges (synthetic ~190ms, replay ~193ms). When allowing selection `auto`, replay picks `attn_v2` and regresses. Single-conn replay reduces p99 by ~20ms vs multi-conn. So two separate effects: a) kernel pick changes raw compute latency b) connection churn + TLS handshakes + Nagle interactions increase tail further.
sam: OK that isolates it. For a proper apples-to-apples benchmark we need to control client-layer variables as first-class bench knobs: keepalive, max-conns, connection reuse pattern, TLS session reuse. Otherwise heuristics that look benign under single-conn will appear worse under multi-conn.
marie: Agreed. I'll add a small test matrix to the CI bench job: for each kernel candidate we run {synthetic, replay-single-conn, replay-multi-conn} and compare p50/p95/p99. Failing thresholds will block kernel rollout.
taylor: On KV cache: I captured a flame at the moment of the spike — frequent KV writes from long sequences triggered compaction path in our LRU store which pauses application threads for ~5-10ms spikes. We need to either make compaction async or add backpressure in batching heuristics to smooth writes.
jon: Could we also adjust batching heuristics so that when sequence-length distribution is wide it favors smaller micro-batches to avoid large KV churn bursts? Might trade throughput for tail but better for p99.
alex: Yeah, we should run Pareto curve sweeps: vary batch target sizes and kernel choice and measure throughput vs p99. I'll run a small hill-climb script (attached command) and post results.
alex: bench command I used: ``` ./bench/run_replay --trace search-traffic-2026-03-10 --mode replay-multi --clients 128 --keepalive true --tls-session-reuse true ``` replace `--mode replay-single` to hold one conn.
marie: Also add a CI check that forces `--tls-session-reuse false` for replay-multi to simulate worst-case (no session reuse) — we saw thorny enterprise customers still hit that.
ci-bot: bench/regress/2060000001: baseline->candidate p99 delta +18% (225ms vs 190ms). Details: https://ci.redwood/bench/2060000001 (artifact: flame-kv-eviction.svg) :warning:
jon: I'll open a small PR that exposes `FORCE_KERNEL` in our local launch config and wires the bench matrix. tagging @marie.
marie: Please also add a small note in the rollout checklist: "verify client connection pattern parity (keepalive, max-conns, tls reuse) before approving kernel switch".
taylor: I'll work on making KV compaction async; shouldn't block inference threads.
sam: For short-term mitigation we can set `tcp_nodelay=true` for replay to see how much Nagle contributed; but the real fix is to standardize the client harness.
alex: Thanks all — priority for today: gate the rollout with the bench matrix, add kernel pin option, and instrument KV eviction metrics. I'll collect the hill-climb results by EOD and post. :thumbsup:
marie: Thanks — sounds good.
alex: (adding note: we should document this in the perf playbook so future bench authors don't get tripped by client config diffs)
marie: Agreed — I'll add a short section under docs/perf/playbook about apples-to-apples and common client-side pitfalls.
ci-bot: CI:bench-matrix job queued for 2060000001.
